text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,291.1, up 0.58% on the day and 1.04% over the last five sessions, while the broader Nifty 500 rose only 0.08% (1.26% five‑day). Advances outnumbered declines (174 vs 316) but the breadth score of 73.6 still signals a “healthy” market. Bank Nifty led the rally, gaining 0.89% (4.21% five‑day). Volatility, measured by India VIX, ticked higher to 15.68 (+1.16%), indicating modest fear despite the rise.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers, adding INR 4,864.68 crore, whereas Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 3,519.05 crore, extending a 13‑day buying streak for FIIs and an 11‑day selling streak for DIIs. The leading sectors were PSU banks, capital markets and FMCG, while IT and media showed weakness. Options data show a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 0.94 for Nifty and 1.24 for Bank Nifty, suggesting slightly more put interest. The Nifty max‑pain level sits at 25,200 with a call wall at 26,000 and a put wall at 25,000; Bank Nifty’s max‑pain is 59,000, call wall 62,000 and put wall 57,000.

Watch the Nifty test around 25,300 (analyst‑cited hurdle) and the 25,197 support (S1). A break below the put wall (25,000) could pull the index toward the lower pivot (25,196). For Bank Nifty, the key levels are 61,288 (S1) and 61,500 (pivot). Global cues – weaker US equity moves and a firm dollar – may keep pressure on the market, while sector rotation toward banks and consumer‑durables could sustain the upside.
